description_good_justification: The README says in its first lines what spec is: the official standards, schemas and guidelines of NovaTrail, an open platform for adaptive learning, interactive lessons and AI tutoring, and what that platform does. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to obtain spec (its releases, which other repositories take as a git submodule, and how to verify one), how to give feedback (GitHub issues) and how to contribute (its Contributing section and the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md). https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec#contributing
contribution_justification: Changes come as GitHub pull requests: an issue first, then a pull request whose every commit is signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin. The branch main takes changes only through pull requests whose checks pass. The process is in the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md, which GitHub shows for this repository: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists what every contribution keeps to (no learners' data, no secrets, the devcontainer, licenses compatible with Apache-2.0, a DCO sign-off) and points to the rules every NovaTrail repository shares, RULES.md, which include the rule on tests: https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/RULES.md
floss_license_justification: Apache-2.0, an OSI-approved license, covers the code, the documents and the module format. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the OSI.
license_location_justification: The license is the top-level file LICENSE: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README says what spec holds and how to take and verify a release. Its Contributing section, and the Environment section of CLAUDE.md in more detail, say how to start (open the repository in its devcontainer) and how to run the checks. RULES.md says what keeps the work safe: everything inside the devcontainer, exact versions checked against their sums, no secrets and no learners' data in the repository. The module format is documented in format/README.md. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec#readme
documentation_interface_justification: spec produces a module format and a set of checks. The format's external interface is its normative text and its JSON Schemas, whose every property has a description: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/format/README.md. The checks are recipes of the justfile, and `just --list` names each with its arguments. The README says what the four checks CI runs check, what they print and how they exit; the comment above each recipe in the justfile says what it takes, prints and returns, and the Environment section of CLAUDE.md names the recipes another repository calls. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/justfile
sites_https_justification: The project's only site is its GitHub repository, served over HTTPS: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, open to anyone with a GitHub account, and nothing to install. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/issues
english_justification: The README, RULES.md, CLAUDE.md, the code, its comments and the normative module format are in English, and issues and pull requests are accepted in English or Russian. The descriptive platform documents under docs/ and the work plan are in Russian, the author's working language.
maintained_justification: Under active development: see the commits and the releases. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/releases
repo_public_justification: A public git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec
repo_track_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, and every commit of a pull request is signed off under the DCO.
repo_interim_justification: Every pull request, its branch and its commits are public before they reach main and a release.
repo_distributed_justification: The repository is git, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version vX.Y.Z, tagged on its commit. The release workflow numbers it, and nobody tags by hand; releases are immutable, so a tag cannot move. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
version_semver_justification: Versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: each release is the next patch of the current line, and a change that gives the module format a new version starts a new line.
version_tags_justification: Each release is the git tag vX.Y.Z, which the release workflow creates together with the release.
release_notes_justification: A release follows every merge to main, and its notes on GitHub list the pull request it brings, linked to the pull request's description: an English summary of what changed and why. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability of spec's own results has been fixed in any release. If one is, its release notes will name it and link its GitHub security advisory.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported as GitHub issues: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/issues
report_tracker_justification: GitHub issues track individual reports. The project's own planned work is in its work plan, RUN.md.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been submitted yet; the maintainer answers each report in its issue.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been submitted yet; the maintainer answers each request in its issue.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public, permanent and searchable: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The security policy, which every repository of the organization shares, says how to report a vulnerability: privately, through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/security/policy
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled: a report goes over HTTPS to the maintainers and opens a draft advisory that only they and the reporter see. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in the last six months.
build_justification: Nothing in spec is compiled for itself: its tools are JavaScript modules that Node runs as they are. Its Go module, which Go code of the platform takes at the tag of a release and builds, is vetted and tested with the Go of the devcontainer, and its zip built as the Go module proxy will build it, on every pull request (`just go-check`); the types of the module format in it are generated from the format's schemas, and CI checks that they are what the schemas give (`just types-check`). What is built is the environment they run in, the toolchain stage of .devcontainer/Dockerfile, from a base image pinned by digest and tools pinned by version and SHA-256; CI rebuilds it on every run. A release also carries the module format as a file, which git archive builds of the released commit (`just release-files`). https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/.devcontainer/Dockerfile
build_common_tools_justification: Docker builds the environment, npm installs the tools' packages from their lock file, the go command vets, tests and builds the Go module, git archive builds the release's files, and just runs every recipe.
build_floss_tools_justification: All FLOSS: Docker Engine (Apache-2.0), Node.js (MIT), npm (Artistic-2.0), Go (BSD-3-Clause), git (GPL-2.0), just (CC0-1.0) and cosign (Apache-2.0), which signs the release's files.
test_justification: The tools have an automated test suite in this repository, under Apache-2.0: Node's built-in test runner over tools/*/test/*.test.mjs, and the go command's own over the Go module and its checks, spec_test.go, tools/gomod/main_test.go and tools/types/roundtrip/main_test.go. `just coverage` runs every test of tools/ and `just go-check` the Go tests; the README says so, and CI runs both on every pull request and on main: https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: `just coverage` runs every test of tools/, `just go-check` the Go tests, and each check has a recipe for its own tests, such as `just docs-check-test`, which `just --list` names; under them are Node's own test runner, `node --test`, and `go test`.
test_most_justification: On 2026-10-26 the tests covered 97% of the lines and 95% of the branches of tools/, as Node measures them. `just coverage` prints the current figures on every run, and Codecov shows its own: https://app.codecov.io/gh/altnovatrail/spec
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs every check and every test on each pull request and on each commit to main, and main takes a pull request only when they pass.
test_policy_justification: RULES.md, the rules every NovaTrail repository shares: code comes with its tests, so a pull request that adds or changes what code does adds or changes the tests of its automated suite. A pull request merges only when at least 90% of its changed lines are covered (codecov/patch, a required check), and `just coverage` fails when no test loads a module of tools/. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/RULES.md
tests_are_added_justification: The latest major changes came with their tests: the task part of the module format, whose rules and open view came with tests of format-check and with examples and test vectors that `just format-check` checks (https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/pull/47); the skill graph and the shared taxonomy, with their examples and test vectors (#46); the badges of the README, with a test that checks them against the documented list (#39).
tests_documented_added_justification: The rule on tests is in RULES.md, which the organization's CONTRIBUTING.md names as the rules every contribution follows.
warnings_justification: Every file of tools/ is an ES module and so runs in JavaScript's strict mode; the bash recipes run with `set -euo pipefail`; `go vet` checks the Go code on every pull request, as `just go-check` runs it. SonarCloud analyses the code on every pull request, and its quality gate is a required check. https://sonarcloud.io/summary/new_code?id=altnovatrail_spec
warnings_fixed_justification: A finding of SonarCloud or CodeQL is fixed in code before the next task starts; marking one false is a last resort, with the reason written down. SonarCloud's current findings are public: https://sonarcloud.io/project/issues?id=altnovatrail_spec
warnings_strict_justification: SonarCloud's quality gate holds a merge on any new finding, and the answer to a finding is a change to the code.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designs for least privilege, fail-safe defaults and a small attack surface. Every workflow starts with a read-only token, and a job gets only the write it needs: the release job to publish the release, the analyses to upload their results, and the coverage and Scorecard jobs an OIDC token to show who uploads; the workflows hold no secret. The branch main has no bypass, and a merge waits for the checks of the documents and tools, the secret scan, the DCO sign-off, CodeQL, SonarCloud and codecov/patch. Inputs are checked against allowlists: the module format's schemas reject any field they do not name, the documents check takes no path from its command line, and the licenses check refuses a lock file outside its repository. The decisions behind these, in Russian, are in https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/blob/main/docs/decisions.md
know_common_errors_justification: For this kind of software, checks that read a repository and the workflows of its CI, the maintainer counters: script injection and untrusted checkouts in workflows (none, and Scorecard's Dangerous-Workflow check scores 10); supply-chain tampering (actions and shared workflows pinned by commit, downloads checked against SHA-256 sums pinned in the file); path traversal (paths resolved and kept inside the repository); commands that a repository's git configuration can run (the documents check, which also reads other repositories, runs git with core.fsmonitor off); YAML pitfalls such as implicit types (the format's YAML rules); and instructions hidden in data for an AI model (a module is data, never instructions, and a program decides every verdict).
crypto_published_justification: spec implements no cryptography. It relies on SHA-256, published and reviewed (FIPS 180-4): the devcontainer and CI check every archive they download against a SHA-256 sum pinned in the file, and the module format names a module's package by the SHA-256 of its canonical text (format/README.md, section 25), which format-check computes for the vectors of packages. The release signs its files with cosign, keyless, through Sigstore, whose certificates and signatures are ECDSA, also published and reviewed (FIPS 186-5).
crypto_call_justification: It calls sha256sum, Node.js's node:crypto and cosign, and never implements cryptography itself.
crypto_floss_justification: sha256sum is part of GNU coreutils, node:crypto is Node.js's set of wrappers for OpenSSL's functions (Node.js 24 documentation, Crypto, read 2026-10-28), and cosign is Sigstore's, under Apache-2.0: all of them are FLOSS.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is used: SHA-256 only.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No algorithm with known serious weaknesses is used: SHA-256 only, never SHA-1 or MD5.
crypto_pfs_justification: spec implements no key agreement; its downloads go over HTTPS, through curl and git.
crypto_random_justification: spec generates no keys or nonces.
delivery_mitm_justification: spec is delivered over HTTPS only: the repository, its releases and their files, the git submodule other repositories take it as, and its Go module, through the Go module proxy, whose checksum database holds each version to its bytes. Releases are immutable, GitHub attests each one with its files, which `gh release verify` and `gh release verify-asset` check, and each file is signed with cosign, its bundle beside it in the release.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP: every SHA-256 sum is pinned in the file next to its version, and every download in spec's files is restricted to HTTPS, redirects included (curl --proto =https --proto-redir =https).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability is open. Dependabot has raised no alert for spec; when Scorecard's Vulnerabilities check found four advisories in fast-uri, a dependency of the tools, published on 2026-10-23, the fix came on 2026-10-26. https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/commit/f7775296222620d87f9530182595141215f1deab
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Dependabot security updates are on, and a finding of Scorecard, CodeQL or SonarCloud is fixed before the next task starts.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the whole history on every pull request and on main, and GitHub's secret scanning and push protection are on. The workflows hold no secret: coverage goes to Codecov with a short-lived OIDC token.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, with the security-extended queries, analyses the JavaScript of tools/, the Go of the Go module and its check, and every workflow, and SonarCloud analyses the repository, on every pull request and on main. Both are required checks, and a release comes only after CI passes on main.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-extended queries and SonarCloud's security rules look for common vulnerabilities. SonarCloud found, and the pull requests fixed before they merged, a download that could follow a redirect off HTTPS (S6506, #39) and a path taken from the command line (S8705 and S8707, #47).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The ruleset of main holds a merge on any CodeQL alert at error level or of high severity and above, and on SonarCloud's quality gate; every finding is fixed before the next task starts.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and on every commit to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The automated test suite runs on every pull request and on main. On 2026-10-26 it covered 95% of the branches of tools/, above the 80% that the criterion counts as dynamic analysis, and `just coverage` prints the current figure on every run.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: spec has no code in a memory-unsafe language: its tools are JavaScript, and its Go module and its check are Go.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The tools check their own invariants and throw, always on, and the tests assert with node:assert in strict mode.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: A failing test fails a required check, and the pull request cannot merge until it passes. No vulnerability has been found this way.
